label: axillary
definition: A positional quality inhering in a plant structure by virtue of its arising in an axil, the upper angle between a leaf or bract and the stem that bears it.
reason: Matches standard glossary usage (borne in the axil of a leaf or bract). Correct genus. PATO has no axillary class, only relational terms.

label: leaf-opposed
definition: A positional quality inhering in a plant structure by virtue of its arising from the stem on the side opposite the point of attachment of a leaf.
reason: Standard meaning (e.g. Vitaceae tendrils/inflorescences, Piper spikes): borne at a node opposite the leaf. Correct genus, not in PATO.

label: basal
definition: A positional quality inhering in a plant structure by virtue of its arising at or near the base of its supporting stem or shoot system.
reason: Right for 'basal leaves' (radical) and basal inflorescences. PATO:0002349 'basal to' is the relational counterpart, not a duplicate. Note: 'shoot system' as a bearer is odd (a shoot system is not itself basal). Limit rule matching to leaves and inflorescences so that 'basal' meaning 'at the base of an organ' (e.g. basal lobes) is not mapped here.

label: solitary
definition: A spatial pattern quality inhering in a plant structure by virtue of its being borne individually at a particular attachment site rather than together with other structures of the same kind at that site.
reason: Standard usage (flowers solitary in the axils). Sibling of FLOPO paired/fascicled under spatial pattern. Not in PATO.

label: paired
definition: A spatial pattern quality inhering in a plant structure by virtue of its being borne together with one other structure of the same kind as a pair at a common node or closely associated attachment sites.
reason: Correct. PATO:0040024 'bilaterally paired' is about left-right body symmetry, not a duplicate. 'Geminate' fits as a related synonym.

label: rosulate
definition: A spatial pattern quality inhering in a leaf or shoot system by virtue of the leaf belonging to, or the shoot system bearing, a dense radiating cluster of leaves on a shortened axis.
reason: Glossaries apply rosulate both to the leaves (in a rosette) and to the plant (with leaves in a rosette). Both readings name the same arrangement, so this is one meaning seen from the part and from the whole, as with capitate. Not in PATO.

label: capitate
definition: An aggregated quality inhering in an inflorescence or flower by virtue of its flowers forming, or the flower belonging to, a compact head-like cluster on a shortened inflorescence axis.
reason: Arrangement sense (flowers in a head). Correct child of aggregated. The shape sense (capitate stigma or hair) is already split off as FLOPO:0991097 head-shaped, so the bearer limit to inflorescence/flower must stay in the rules.

label: caespitose
definition: An aggregated quality inhering in a whole plant or shoot system by virtue of its stems or shoots growing close together in a dense tuft or clump from the base.
reason: Standard meaning (tufted, growing in dense clumps). 'Cespitose' and 'tufted' are true exact synonyms. Not in PATO (PATO's tufted terms are neuron morphology).

label: creeping
definition: A prostrate quality inhering in a stem or plant by virtue of its growing along the surface of the ground and rooting at the nodes.
reason: Correct for creeping/repent stems and plants (prostrate plus rooting at the nodes), and fits the PATO prostrate definition. Note: floras also say 'creeping rhizome' (growing horizontally below ground). That sense is not prostrate and must not be mapped here; the bearer list correctly leaves out rhizome.

label: mat-forming
definition: A shape quality inhering in a plant by virtue of its growing low and spreading into a dense, flat mat over the ground.
reason: Habit (growth form) quality, treated like the reviewed habit classes palm-like and straggly under shape. The meaning matches glossaries (low, dense, spreading carpet). No better PATO parent: prostrate does not imply density.

label: twiggy
definition: A branched quality inhering in a whole plant or shoot by virtue of its bearing numerous slender, fine branches.
reason: Correct child of branched. 'Much-branched' is only a related synonym (it does not imply slender twigs), which is the right level.

label: leafy
definition: A structural quality inhering in a whole plant or shoot by virtue of its bearing well-developed foliage leaves along its axes.
reason: Matches flora usage ('stems leafy' as opposed to scapose or leafless). Not in PATO. 'Leafy' meaning leaf-like (leafy bracts, i.e. foliaceous) is another sense and should not be mapped here; 'foliose' is acceptable only as a related synonym.

label: subsessile
definition: An attachment quality inhering in a plant structure by virtue of its being attached by a very short stalk, so that it is almost sessile.
reason: Standard meaning. Sibling of PATO:0001436 sessile (sensu botany) under attachment quality. It cannot go under sessile, because it has a stalk.

label: bipinnate
definition: A pinnate quality inhering in a compound leaf by virtue of its primary divisions (pinnae) being themselves pinnate.
reason: Standard meaning (twice pinnately compound), correct child of PATO pinnate, consistent with FLOPO:0991159 tripinnate. Not in PATO.

label: unisexual
definition: A phenotypic sex quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's having functional stamens or functional carpels but not both; in an inflorescence, by virtue of all its flowers being of the same one sex.
reason: The meaning is right and the parent is right (sibling of FLOPO monoecious/dioecious/polygamous; PATO has hermaphrodite but no unisexual). The current text grammatically gives stamens and carpels to the inflorescence itself and mixes the two bearers awkwardly; the new text separates them. 'Imperfect' fits flowers only, which is fine as a related synonym.

label: sweet-scented
definition: An odorous quality inhering in a plant structure by virtue of its having a sweet, pleasant odour.
reason: Correct child of odorous. 'Fragrant' (pleasant scent, not necessarily sweet) is properly only related. Rules should keep bare 'sweet' on fruit out of this class, since there it is a taste.

label: spicy-scented
definition: An odorous quality inhering in a plant structure by virtue of its having a pungent, spicy odour.
reason: Correct. 'Spicy' as a related synonym is acceptable, because in floras it describes scent of flowers and crushed leaves.

label: musty-smelling
definition: An odorous quality inhering in a plant structure by virtue of its having a stale, mouldy odour.
reason: Correct child of odorous; synonyms fit. Not in PATO.

label: sour-smelling
definition: An odorous quality inhering in a plant structure by virtue of its having a sharp, acid odour.
reason: The class and definition are fine. But the related synonym 'sour' (24 source statements) usually describes taste in floras ('fruit sour', 'sour pulp'), which is a flavour (PATO:0000043) quality, not an odour. Drop 'sour' as a synonym, or match it only when an odour word ('smell', 'odour', 'scent') appears nearby.

label: foetid
definition: An odorous quality inhering in a plant structure by virtue of its having an unpleasant, offensive odour.
reason: Standard meaning; fetid/foul-smelling are true synonyms, malodorous properly related. Not in PATO.

label: exfoliating
definition: A texture quality inhering in bark, another surface tissue, or a plant axis bearing that tissue by virtue of its outer layers peeling or shedding in sheets, strips, plates or flakes.
reason: Matches bark descriptions (peeling, flaking). Texture is a reasonable parent. Covering the axis that bears the bark reflects flora usage ('stems exfoliating'). Not in PATO.

label: fissured
definition: A texture quality inhering in bark, another surface, or a plant axis bearing that surface by virtue of its being marked by deep cracks or clefts.
reason: Standard bark term. Correct parent. Not in PATO.

label: petiolate
definition: An attachment quality inhering in a leaf by virtue of its being attached to its supporting shoot axis by a petiole.
reason: The definition and parent are correct (opposite of PATO:0001436 sessile (sensu botany)). But the exact synonym 'stalked leaf' names a part plus a quality, not a quality. Replace it with 'stalked' as a related synonym (stalked is wider than petiolate) and keep 'petioled'.

label: ovate
definition: A 2-D shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's outline being egg-shaped, entirely convex and broadest below the middle, towards the base.
reason: Correct plane (flat) ovate, the standard leaf-outline term. Not a duplicate: PATO:0001891 'ovate' is a 3-D spheroid. This is the temporary class awaiting PATO PR #627 (plane ovate PATO:0104368, unmerged); replace it when the PR is merged.

label: obovoid
definition: A spheroid quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being egg-shaped and broadest above the middle, with the narrow end towards the base.
reason: Correct solid shape (the 3-D form of obovate); spheroid is the right parent, matching PATO:0001891. This is the temporary class awaiting PATO PR #627 (obovoid PATO:0104369, unmerged); replace it when the PR is merged.

label: fibrous
definition: A texture quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's consisting largely of tough, thread-like fibres.
reason: Two meanings joined by 'or': containing tough fibres (leaf, stem texture) and splitting into fibres (fibrous, shredding bark). Keep the first here. Shredding into fibres is a separate bark quality. No PATO class: PATO:0002134 fibrillary and PATO:0001667-type fibrotic terms are cell and pathology terms.

label: fibrous-rooted
definition: A structure quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's consisting of many slender roots of about equal thickness, arising from the stem base, without a dominant taproot.
reason: The text says 'A branched quality' but the parent is PATO:0000141 structure. The defining trait is many roots of equal thickness, not branching, so PATO:0000402 branched is not the right genus. The bearer is the root system, not a single root.

label: beaked
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's apex being prolonged into a narrow, beak-like point.
reason: Meaning and the synonym rostrate are correct, and PATO has no beaked or rostrate. Only the wording changes to the standard form.

label: horned
reason: Correct (cornute). PATO:0002161 bicornuate is a narrower two-horned term used for the uterus. It is not a duplicate.

label: zigzag
definition: A bent quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being bent alternately in opposite directions along its length, usually at the nodes.
reason: Zigzag is a kind of PATO:0000617 bent ('having one or more angles in its length'), so the parent should be bent, not shape. The synonym fractiflex fits.

label: umbelliform
reason: Correct, and it matches the sibling resemblance terms raceme-like FLOPO:0991197 and PATO:0002455 corymb-like. No PATO duplicate.

label: medium-sized
reason: Means the middle of the usual size range for that kind of part ('a medium-sized tree'). PATO:0045050 normal size means 'not abnormal' compared with a reference, which is a different meaning, so it is not a duplicate.

label: pectinate
reason: Correct comb-like sense. No PATO class.

label: indeterminate
reason: Correct botanical sense for an inflorescence. No PATO class. 'monopodial' is fine as a related synonym only.

label: subterranean
reason: Correct. hypogeous (exact) and hypogeal (related, mostly said of germination) fit. No PATO class.

label: aerial
reason: Correct, the opposite of subterranean (aerial roots, aerial stems). No PATO class.

label: androgynous
definition: A phenotypic sex quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's bearing both staminate and pistillate flowers, the staminate above the pistillate on the same axis.
reason: The botanical term (e.g. androgynous spikes in Carex) means staminate flowers at the top and pistillate below; the opposite is gynaecandrous. The current text only says 'both kinds of flowers', which is too wide and overlaps monoecious FLOPO:0991071.

label: virgate
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being long, slender, straight and erect, like a wand.
reason: Meaning is right but the text is not in 'inhering in ... by virtue of' form and it mixes the axis with the branching system. 'broom-like' stays a related synonym only.

label: palm-like
reason: Whole-plant habit, defined correctly. No PATO class. 'palm' as a related synonym is a weak noun match but acceptable.

label: claw-shaped
reason: Correct (unguiform). Do not confuse it with FLOPO:0991169 clawed (unguiculate), a base narrowed into a stalk. The two are distinct.

label: pea-sized
definition: A size quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being about the size of a pea.
reason: Meaning is right. The text is not in standard form and includes a note ('without a fixed numerical diameter') that belongs in a comment.

label: cherry-like
reason: Already obsolete, and rightly so. It joins size, shape (globose) and texture (fleshy, PATO:0002351) in one class. Annotate the parts separately and keep it obsolete.

label: straggly
reason: Correct habit term. No PATO class.

label: submerged
reason: Correct. Matches its siblings aquatic FLOPO:0991112 and terrestrial FLOPO:0991111. No PATO class.

label: floating
reason: Correct for floating leaves and free-floating plants. No PATO class.

label: membranous
definition: A texture quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being thin, soft and flexible, like a membrane.
reason: Too narrow: membranous parts are often but not always translucent, so translucency should not be required. Also not in standard form. No PATO class.

label: scarious
definition: A texture quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being thin, dry and membranous, not green, and often translucent.
reason: The related synonym 'papery' is an EXACT synonym of PATO:0104010 papyraceous, so text matching would hit both. Drop it here. Also give the definition in standard form and add 'not green'.

label: pilose
definition: A hairy quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being covered with long, soft, rather straight, scattered hairs.
reason: PATO files its hair-covering values (tomentose, setose, bristly, etc.) under PATO:0000454 hairy. pilosity is the general attribute, so the parent should be hairy. The related synonym 'hairy' is the PATO class label and should be dropped.

label: puberulous
definition: A pubescent hair quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being covered with very short, fine, soft hairs, barely visible without a lens.
reason: Puberulous means minutely pubescent, so it is a child of PATO:0001320 pubescent hair, not a direct child of pilosity. Synonyms are fine.

label: hirsute
definition: A hairy quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being covered with rather long, coarse, stiff hairs.
reason: Meaning is right, but like the other hair-covering values it belongs under PATO:0000454 hairy. No PATO hirsute class exists.

label: villous
reason: Standard glossary sense (long, soft, often shaggy, not matted hairs); correct pilosity child; no PATO term for villous; villose is an exact variant.

label: glabrescent
reason: Matches the main glossary sense (becoming glabrous with age); glabrate correctly kept as related because some authors use it for 'nearly glabrous'. No PATO equivalent (PATO:0000453 glabrous is the end state).

label: subglabrous
reason: Correct degree term between glabrous (PATO:0000453) and sparsely hairy; no PATO term; pilosity parent is right.

label: mucronate
reason: Correct botanical sense (apex ending abruptly in a short stiff point, the mucro); no PATO term; shape parent consistent with other apex shapes.

label: mucronulate
definition: A mucronate quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's apex ending abruptly in a minute mucro.
reason: A minute mucro is still a mucro, so mucronulate is a subclass of FLOPO:0991054 mucronate, not a sibling under shape. The related synonym 'mucronate' is the label of FLOPO:0991054 and should be removed; otherwise text matching is ambiguous.

label: obcordate
reason: Correct: inversely heart-shaped, with the notch at the apex and the narrow end at the attachment. PATO has only PATO:0000948 heart shaped (cordate), not obcordate; 2-D shape parent is right for a leaf/petal outline.

label: lyrate
definition: A lobed quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being pinnately lobed or divided, with a large rounded terminal lobe and lateral lobes that become smaller towards the base.
reason: The meaning is right, but lyrate is a kind of pinnate lobing, so its parent should be PATO:0001979 lobed rather than generic shape. FLOPO:0991078 pinnatifid would be too narrow because lyrate blades can be divided to the midrib.

label: scabrous
definition: A rough quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's surface being rough to the touch because of minute stiff projections or very short stiff hairs.
reason: Meaning is correct, but PATO:0000700 rough (irregular surface texture) exists and scabrous is a kind of rough; it should be placed under rough, not directly under texture. Synonyms (scabrid exact; scaberulous, scabridulous related diminutives) are fine.

label: papillose
reason: Class and definition are right (surface bearing papillae). The related synonym 'papillary' is the label of PATO:0002108, which means resembling a nipple-like projection (is_a exserted), a different sense; remove it to avoid mis-mapping.

label: tuberculate
definition: A rough quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's surface bearing small rounded wart-like protuberances (tubercles).
reason: A tubercle-covered surface is a kind of PATO:0000700 rough (sibling of PATO:0001361 warty). The related synonym 'verrucose' means warty and should map to PATO:0001361 warty, not to this class (FLOPO:0991088 verruculose already sits nearby).

label: sulcate
reason: Correct: longitudinally grooved/furrowed; PATO:0001948 furrowed (two or more parallel channels) is the right parent. 'grooved' (PATO:0002255 label) as a related synonym is broader but not wrong.

label: ribbed
reason: Correct sense (prominent longitudinal ribs); costate is a standard exact synonym; PATO:0002358 ridged is the closest PATO parent.

label: imbricate
reason: Correct: a pattern of a set of overlapping parts (bracts, scales, perianth in bud). PATO:0002488 overlapping is a two-entity relational quality, so spatial pattern of the set is the better parent.

label: appressed
reason: Correct glossary sense (lying close and flat against another structure, e.g. hairs, leaves on stem); adpressed is an exact variant; no PATO term.

label: stipitate
reason: Correct; it is the opposite of PATO:0001436 sessile (sensu botany), which has the same parent attachment quality. No PATO term for stalked.

label: connate
definition: A fused with quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being united by tissue fusion with other structures of the same kind.
reason: Connate is fusion of like parts; PATO:0000642 fused with exists and FLOPO:0991129 adnate (fusion of unlike parts) is already under it. Connate should be its sibling there, not directly under attachment quality.

label: free
reason: Correct botanical sense (not fused to like or unlike parts). PATO:0000651 unfused from means 'no longer merged' (a separation event), so it is not an equivalent; attachment quality is acceptable, like PATO:0001436 sessile.

label: concolorous
definition: A color pattern quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's compared surfaces or parts having the same colour.
reason: Meaning is right, but this compares colours across parts or surfaces, which is PATO:0000019 color pattern (relative position of hues), not the single composite colour PATO:0000014.

label: discolorous
definition: A color pattern quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's compared surfaces or parts, typically the two leaf surfaces, having different colours.
reason: Parent should be PATO:0000019 color pattern (as for concolorous). The related synonym 'discolored' is the label of PATO:0000331 (altered or spoiled in colour), a different meaning; remove it.

label: monoecious
definition: A phenotypic sex quality inhering in a plant by virtue of its bearing separate staminate and pistillate (or male and female) reproductive structures on the same individual.
reason: Class and parent are right; the text names the wrong genus ('reproductive quality') and restricts to seed plants. Brought in line with FLOPO:0991177 polygamous.

label: dioecious
definition: A phenotypic sex quality inhering in a plant by virtue of its bearing only staminate or only pistillate (male or female) reproductive structures, the two sexes occurring on different individuals.
reason: Wrong genus in the text ('reproductive quality'); 'belonging to a sexual system' describes the species, not the bearer. Brought in line with FLOPO:0991177 polygamous.

label: unifoliolate
definition: A structure quality inhering in a leaf by virtue of its being a compound leaf reduced to a single leaflet, whose blade is jointed to the petiole by a petiolule or articulation.
reason: Meaning and parent are right (sibling of FLOPO:0991161 trifoliolate), but 'distinguished from a simple leaf by its compound-leaf organization' is circular; the diagnostic feature is the joint between leaflet and petiole.

label: extra-axillary
reason: Correct glossary sense (arising outside the axil, e.g. inflorescences in Solanaceae and Vitaceae); no PATO term; position parent right.

label: resinous
definition: A coating quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's surface being covered with resin, a viscous plant secretion that hardens on exposure.
reason: The definition is not genus-differentia and mixes two meanings: containing or producing resin internally, and a resin-coated surface. Only the surface sense is a texture; it belongs under PATO:0002012 coating. The related synonym 'adhesive' is PATO:0002331, and sticky surfaces are PATO:0001370 viscid, so remove it.

label: subcoriaceous
definition: A texture quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being somewhat leathery, tougher than chartaceous but thinner or less rigid than coriaceous (PATO:0104032).
reason: PATO:0104032 coriaceous now exists (requested for FLOPO, under texture). Subcoriaceous is not a subclass of it (it is less than coriaceous), so keep it as a texture sibling, but refer the definition to the PATO term.

label: turbinate
definition: An obconical quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being shaped like a spinning top: broad and rounded at the distal end and tapering to a narrow base.
reason: PATO:0002347 obconical (a cone with the pointed end at the attachment) already exists; turbinate is its top-shaped special case, so the parent should be obconical, not 3-D shape. 'obconical' cannot stay a related synonym because it is the label of a PATO class; remove it.

label: pinnatifid
definition: A pinnately lobed quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being cut pinnately into lobes, with the sinuses reaching about halfway or more towards the midrib but not to it.
reason: Plain 'shape' is too broad. FLOPO:0991157 pinnately lobed (under PATO:0001979 lobed) now exists, along with its siblings pinnatipartite and pinnatisect (FLOPO:0991156, FLOPO:0991155). Pinnatifid is the shallower depth grade, so it belongs under pinnately lobed. Not PATO:0000410 pinnate, which is about leaflets. Many floras use pinnatifid loosely to mean pinnately lobed, so watch for overlap.

label: canescent
definition: A hairy quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being covered with fine, short grey or whitish hairs that give its surface a grey-white appearance.
reason: The meaning is correct (grey-hairy, hoary) but the text is not in PATO form. Suggest PATO:0000454 hairy as the parent: pilosity also covers glabrous, and bearded (FLOPO:0991118) was placed under hairy.

label: divaricate
definition: A spreading quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's diverging at a wide angle, approaching a right angle, from the axis that bears it.
reason: Divaricate is an orientation (widely spreading), not a spatial pattern. PATO:0104356 spreading (an orientation, 'directed outward and diverging from a principal axis') is the right parent. 'widely spreading' can be an exact synonym.

label: serrulate
definition: A serrated quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's margin bearing very small, sharp, forward-pointing teeth.
reason: PATO:0001206 serrated (sharp teeth pointing to the apex) exists; serrulate is its fine-toothed special case, so it should be a child of serrated, not of shape.

label: accrescent
definition: A structural quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's continuing to grow and enlarge after the stage at which comparable organs stop growing, as a calyx that enlarges after flowering.
reason: The meaning is correct; the text is rewritten into PATO form. PATO has no good parent for a non-pathological organ that keeps enlarging (the growth qualities are for processes), so 'structure' is acceptable.

label: valvate
definition: A spatial pattern quality inhering in a set of structures, typically perianth parts in bud, by virtue of their adjacent members meeting edge to edge without overlapping.
reason: The text names the genus 'aestivation quality', but the parent is spatial pattern, and it covers only the perianth (valvate also applies to bracts and to bud scales). It is the counterpart of FLOPO:0991063 imbricate. In floras, 'valvate' also means 'opening by valves' (capsules, anthers); keep that sense out of this class.

label: multiseriate
definition: A spatial pattern quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's members or component parts being arranged in more than two rows, series or whorls.
reason: Correct meaning; rewritten into PATO form so that it also fits a hair made of several rows of cells and a perianth in several whorls.

label: bilabiate
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's limb being divided into two distinct lips, an upper and a lower.
reason: Correct meaning and parent (PATO has no two-lipped term); the text is not in PATO form.

label: strigose
definition: A hairy quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's surface bearing stiff, straight, sharp hairs that lie closely appressed and point in one direction.
reason: Correct meaning; the text is not in PATO form. Suggest PATO:0000454 hairy as the parent, as for bearded.

label: barbellate
definition: A texture quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's surface bearing minute, backward-pointing barbs, as on a pappus bristle or awn.
reason: The text says 'surface quality', but the parent is texture; rewritten in PATO form.

label: verruculose
definition: A warty quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's surface bearing very small wart-like projections.
reason: PATO:0001361 warty (a texture quality) exists; verruculose means 'minutely warty', so it should be a child of warty, not of texture.

label: biseriate
definition: A spatial pattern quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's members or component parts being arranged in two rows, series or whorls.
reason: Correct meaning; rewritten into PATO form so that it also fits hairs made of two rows of cells and a perianth in two whorls.

label: uniseriate
definition: A spatial pattern quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's members or component parts being arranged in a single row, series or whorl.
reason: Correct meaning. Most flora uses are about a hair made of a single row of cells, where the hair is the bearer, not its cells; the rewrite covers this.

label: strigulose
definition: A strigose quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's appressed stiff hairs being very short and fine.
reason: Strigulose means 'minutely strigose', so it should be a child of FLOPO:0991086 strigose, not of pilosity directly.

label: dimorphic
definition: A morphology quality inhering in a set of structures of the same kind, in one plant or one taxon, by virtue of its members occurring in two distinct forms.
reason: Correct meaning and parent; rewritten into PATO form. PATO:0002451 sexually dimorphic is the narrower, sex-linked case and does not replace this class (dimorphic leaves, dimorphic fronds, dimorphic achenes).

label: autoicous
definition: A phenotypic sex quality inhering in a bryophyte gametophyte by virtue of its bearing male and female gametoecia on separate branches of the same individual.
reason: Correct meaning (a kind of monoicous); the text has the genus 'reproductive quality' and is not in PATO form.

label: andromonoecious
definition: A phenotypic sex quality inhering in a plant by virtue of its bearing both staminate flowers and bisexual flowers on the same individual.
reason: Correct meaning; the genus 'reproductive quality' does not match the parent. Not a child of FLOPO:0991071 monoecious, which needs pistillate flowers.

label: acute (sensu botany)
reason: The botanical sense (sides meeting at less than 90 degrees, not drawn out) is correct. PATO:0000389 acute is a process quality (sudden onset), so the sensu label is needed. 'pointed' is an acceptable parent.

label: subacute (sensu botany)
reason: Correct botanical sense (only slightly acute, angle near 90 degrees). PATO:0002091 subacute is a time-course quality of a process, so the sensu label is needed.

label: head-shaped
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being abruptly enlarged at its tip into a rounded head.
reason: The class is sound, but the synonyms do not fit. 'capitellate' means 'with a small head' and should be a related or narrower synonym, not exact. The usual word for stigmas and hairs is 'capitate', but FLOPO:0991006 capitate means clustered flowers, so add 'capitate (stigma, hair)' as a related synonym with care.

label: fascicled
definition: An aggregated quality inhering in a set of structures by virtue of their being borne in a close cluster arising from about the same point.
reason: The parent should be PATO:0001629 aggregated (exact synonym 'clustered'), as for capitate and caespitose. Also, PATO:0001861 fasciculated has 'fascicled' as an EXACT synonym in the sense of a bundle of nerve or muscle fibres; the label clashes and needs a sensu-botany label or a note.

label: cartilaginous (sensu botany)
reason: Correct botanical sense (hard, tough and somewhat flexible, like cartilage). PATO:0001449 cartilaginous is about the amount of cartilage tissue, so a separate sensu-botany class is justified.

label: reticulate
definition: A spatial pattern quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being marked by, or composed of, a network of veins, ridges or walls.
reason: The class itself is acceptable: a structural network, unlike PATO:0001947 netted, which is a colour pattern. But the exact synonym 'net-veined' covers only venation, while the bearers include bark, pollen and seed; make it a narrower synonym. PATO already lists 'reticulated' as an exact synonym of netted, so add a note to keep the two apart.

label: unequal
reason: Matches the 2026-11-13 decision: a size quality of a set of like parts (sepals, glumes, stamens). PATO has no such term; PATO:0001227 variant is not about size. 'Leaf base unequal' (oblique) is a different meaning and belongs to asymmetry, not to this class.

label: equal
reason: Correct counterpart of FLOPO:0991101 unequal. It is a quality of a set of like parts, so it deliberately departs from the bearer's-X form. Neither PATO size (PATO:0000117) nor any other PATO class covers equality within a set. The PATO question noted in the previous review still stands.

label: depressed
definition: A flattened quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being flattened from the apex towards the base, so that it is broader than high.
reason: Two meanings in one class. On fruits, seeds, ovaries and tubers 'depressed' (depressed-globose) means flattened from above; that is close to PATO:0000409 oblate (equatorial diameter greater than polar diameter), so it can stay a FLOPO child of flattened or map to oblate. On a leaf midvein or a stigma 'depressed' means sunk below the surrounding surface, which is PATO:0002416 sunken. Restrict the class to the shape sense and send the midvein and stigma uses to sunken.

label: urceolate
reason: Standard glossary sense (urn-shaped: inflated below, contracted at the mouth, often with a short flaring limb). It sits correctly under concave 3-D shape beside cup-shaped and trumpet-shaped, and PATO has no urceolate class.

label: sheathing
definition: A clasping quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's base or lower part being extended into a sheath that wraps round the axis to which it is attached, with its margins meeting, overlapping or fused.
reason: The meaning and parent are right. But 'forming a tube that completely surrounds' is too narrow: many sheaths (e.g. grass and many monocot leaf sheaths) are open, with overlapping rather than fused margins, and are still called sheathing.

label: dull
reason: Correct: it is the opposite of PATO:0001373 glistening, under reflectivity. PATO's 'dull' is only a related synonym of a colour-saturation term, so this is not a duplicate. The synonyms matt and matte fit.

label: peltate
reason: Standard sense (stalk attached inside the margin on the lower surface). An attachment quality is a suitable parent, and peltate stigmas and scales fit the same sense. PATO has no peltate class.

label: climbing
reason: The definition matches glossary 'scandent/climbing' and covers leaning, twining and clinging climbers. Scrambling as a related synonym (not exact) is right. Placing it under position follows erect and prostrate, so it is consistent with the other growth-habit classes.

label: tuberous
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being thickened and swollen like a tuber, usually as a storage organ.
reason: The meaning and parent are right, but 'irregularly swollen' is too narrow: tuberous roots are often regularly fusiform or ellipsoid (e.g. Dahlia, Asphodelus).

label: epiphytic
definition: A position quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's growing upon another plant for support, without drawing water or nutrients from it.
reason: The meaning is right but the text breaks the standard 'in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's' form. 'Not organically connected' is vaguer than the usual glossary contrast with parasites, and 'not parasitic' is clearer.

label: terrestrial
definition: A position quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's growing on land, rooted in the soil, rather than in water or upon another plant.
reason: The meaning is right. The rewrite brings the text into the standard form and states the contrast with aquatic and epiphytic, which is how floras use the word.

label: aquatic
definition: A position quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's growing in water, either wholly or partly submerged or floating on its surface.
reason: The meaning is right, but the text is not in the standard form and 'living in water' is unclear for plant parts (an aquatic leaf is a submerged or floating leaf). The rewrite covers both the whole-plant and the leaf uses.

label: sinuate
reason: Glossary sense: a margin with strong in-plane waves, as distinct from undulate (out of plane). It is not a duplicate of PATO:0001989 sinuous, which is a curvature quality of an elongate bearer with many turns, not an edge shape.

label: spirally arranged
reason: Correct phyllotaxis sense, a sibling of distichous and opposite. It is not PATO:0000404 coiled (synonym 'spiral'), which is the shape of a single bearer, so 'spiral (sensu botany)' as a related synonym is appropriate.

label: lacerate
reason: Standard glossary sense (irregularly cut as if torn), under edge shape beside fringed. PATO has no lacerate class.

label: laciniate
reason: Standard sense (cut into narrow, irregular, pointed lobes). Split is a fitting parent beside dissected and multifid, and PATO has no laciniate class.

label: cauline
reason: Correct: borne on the stem as opposed to basal or radical. It is the monadic counterpart of PATO:0002350 cauline to. Odd bearers such as 'stem' are an annotation matter, not a fault of the class.

label: bearded
reason: Matches glossary barbate/bearded (long hairs in a tuft, line or zone, e.g. corolla throat, anther). It is a correct child of hairy, and PATO has no bearded class.

label: cucullate
definition: A concave 3-D shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being hood-shaped: concave, with the apex or the sides arched forward over the concave face.
reason: The meaning and parent are right, but 'shaped like a hood' only restates the exact synonym hooded. The rewrite gives the differentia used in glossaries.

label: trigonous
reason: The definition matches standard use (three-angled with obtuse angles and flat or convex faces), and the convex 3-D shape parent fits. Minor: triquetrous (sharp angles, concave faces) is a different shape, is not convex, and would be better dropped as a synonym rather than kept as related.

label: included
reason: Correct opposite of PATO:0000623 exserted, used for stamens, styles and fruits within the corolla or calyx. PATO:0005016 surrounded by is relational, so it is not a duplicate.

label: bullate
reason: Standard sense (puckered with blister-like bulges between the veins). Surface feature shape is the right parent, and it is correctly kept apart from PATO blistered.

label: conduplicate
reason: Standard sense (folded once lengthwise along the midrib with the adaxial faces together), as a child of folded beside plicate. PATO has no conduplicate class.

label: setaceous
reason: Standard sense (bristle-like), under linear beside subulate. It is correctly distinguished from PATO:0002289 setose (bearing bristles).

label: rotate
reason: Standard sense (wheel-shaped; lobes spreading flat from a very short tube), a sibling of campanulate and funnel-shaped. It is not PATO:0001599 rotated, which is an orientation.

label: corky
reason: Matches glossary corky/suberose (having the light, spongy, elastic texture of cork). Texture is a fitting parent, and PATO has no corky class.

label: scurfy
reason: This matches the glossary sense: covered with small, loose, bran-like scales. The parent 'scaly' (a texture covered with scales) fits, and PATO has no scurfy term. 'Furfuraceous' is used in exactly the same sense in most glossaries, so it could be raised from a related synonym to an exact synonym.

label: anastomosing
definition: A branched quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's branches, or the bearer and other structures of its kind, joining one another to form loops or a network.
bearers: vascular bundle|secondary leaf vein|leaf|lateral leaf vein|leaflet|fruit
reason: The meaning is right, but the most common use is 'lateral veins anastomosing', where the veins themselves join one another (often in loops near the margin), not branches of one vein. The current text is too narrow for that. PATO has no matching term; PATO 'netted' is a colour pattern.

label: adnate
reason: This is the standard sense: fused to an organ of a different kind, as opposed to connate (FLOPO:0991067, same kind). 'Fused with' is a suitable parent, and PATO has no adnate term.

label: gibbous
reason: This matches the glossaries: swollen or pouched on one side, often at the base. PATO 'swollen' is not a good parent because it means a temporary abnormal enlargement. 'Shape' is the right parent.

label: superior (sensu botany)
reason: The definition is correct for a superior ovary, and wording it for an ovary follows the accepted style of 'half-inferior' and 'axile'. The class should only be used with ovary or gynoecium bearers. 'Radicle superior' (the direction of the radicle in the seed) is a different meaning. 'Perianth superior' means the opposite: the perianth sits on top of an inferior ovary. Neither may be mapped here.

label: inferior (sensu botany)
reason: The definition is correct for an inferior ovary (enclosed in and fused with the receptacle or hypanthium). As with 'superior', it should only be used with ovary bearers. 'Radicle inferior' and 'perianth/calyx inferior' mean something else; 'calyx inferior' implies a superior ovary.

label: half-inferior
reason: This is the standard sense, the synonym 'semi-inferior' fits, and the use is already limited to ovary context words.

label: dorsifixed
reason: Correct and in the standard form. It is mainly used for anthers fixed to the filament by their back, and the general wording also covers sori and stipules. 'Attachment quality' is the right parent.

label: basifixed
reason: Correct and in the standard form. It applies to anthers, scales and bracts attached by their base.

label: versatile
reason: This matches the glossary sense: an anther attached near its middle that swings freely on the filament. Wording it for anthers follows the accepted style. Uses with fruit or petal bearers are parsing errors and should not be mapped.

label: heterostylous
definition: A morphology quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's flowers occurring in two or three forms that differ in the relative lengths of the styles and stamens, each plant bearing flowers of one form only.
reason: The meaning is right, but saying a quality inheres in a flower 'by virtue of belonging to a species' is not genus-differentia and names the wrong kind of bearer. Heterostyly describes a plant or taxon whose individuals differ in their flower forms. The rewrite states the differentia directly.

label: buttressed
reason: This matches standard usage: the trunk base has flattened, plank-like flanges running out into the roots. Wording it for a trunk or stem is acceptable. Uses with filament or fruit bearers are parsing errors.

label: muricate
reason: This matches the glossaries: roughened by short, hard, sharp points. 'Rough' (a texture quality) is the right parent, and PATO has no muricate term.

label: saccate
reason: This is the standard sense (pouch- or bag-shaped). 'Concave 3-D shape' (a shape with a cavity) fits, and the synonym 'pouched' fits.

label: petaloid
definition: A morphology quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's resembling a petal in being thin, soft-textured and usually brightly coloured.
reason: In botanical usage, petaloid sepals, bracts or staminodes look like petals in colour and texture, not in outline shape. So 'shape' is the wrong parent, and the definition ('similarity to the appearance of a petal') is vague. Morphology is the nearest fitting parent.

label: spike-like
reason: This is the standard sense of 'spiciform' (resembling a spike, an unbranched inflorescence of sessile flowers), and the synonym fits. Uses with sporangium or operculum bearers should be checked when mapped.

label: scale-like
reason: Correct: small, thin, flat and often appressed, as in scale-like leaves and bracts. PATO has no such term.

label: salverform
reason: This matches the glossaries: a slender tube that expands abruptly into a flat, spreading limb. 'Hypocrateriform' and 'salver-shaped' are correct exact synonyms.

label: inflexed
reason: This is the standard sense (bent inward, towards the axis). 'Bent' (having an angle along its length) is a suitable parent.

label: secund
definition: A positional quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being borne on, or turned towards, one side of the axis that bears it, together with the other structures of its kind.
reason: Glossaries define secund as all borne on one side of the axis, or all turned to one side. The current text only covers 'turned' and so is too narrow. The parent 'position' fits.

label: connivent
reason: This is the standard sense (converging and touching but not fused). It is properly distinguished from 'coherent' (FLOPO:0991187) and 'connate' (FLOPO:0991067).

label: crisped
reason: This matches the glossary sense for margins (finely and irregularly curled or wavy). PATO 'curled' has an unclear definition about parallel chains and is not a better target. 'Crisped' on a stem usually describes its hairs, so those uses should be mapped to a hair bearer, not to the stem margin.

label: dehiscent
reason: This is the standard sense (opening at maturity along definite lines or pores to release the contents). PATO has no dehiscent term, and 'structure' is an acceptable parent. Bearers such as stipule or leaf sheath are probably parsing errors.

label: circumscissile
reason: The definition is correct, but circumscissile is a kind of dehiscence. It should be a subclass of the FLOPO class 'dehiscent' (FLOPO:0991149), not sit directly under 'structure'. As it stands, a reasoner would not infer that a circumscissile fruit is dehiscent.

label: septicidal
reason: The definition is correct, and its own curation note already calls it 'a kind of dehiscent (FLOPO)', but its parent is 'structure' (PATO:0000141). It should be a subclass of 'dehiscent' (FLOPO:0991149). Loculicidal (FLOPO:0991152) and poricidal (FLOPO:0991153) have the same issue.

label: loculicidal
definition: A dehiscent quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's opening at maturity along the middle of the outer wall of each locule, between the septa.
reason: Definition is right, but the parent is PATO:0000141 structure while the class is a kind of the FLOPO dehiscent class (FLOPO:0991149, opening at maturity along a definite line or pore). Its own curation note says so. Move it under dehiscent, alongside septicidal and poricidal.

label: poricidal
definition: A dehiscent quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's opening at maturity by pores or short slits at the apex or on the walls.
reason: Same as loculicidal: it should sit under FLOPO:0991149 dehiscent, not PATO:0000141 structure. Bearers (anthers as in Solanum and Ericaceae, capsules as in Papaver) fit. The definition can stay, apart from the parent wording.

label: jointed
definition: A structural quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's having one or more joints at which it readily separates.
reason: Matches glossary usage of jointed/articulate for pedicels, petioles, stems and lomentaceous fruits. PATO has only the relational 'articulated with' (PATO:0002278), which is not the same thing. Synonyms fit.

label: pinnatisect
definition: A dissected quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being cut to the midrib into segments arranged on either side of it, the segments not stalked.
reason: Standard meaning: cut to the midrib, with the segments not stalked (which separates it from pinnate). This fits under PATO dissected (divided by incisions into distinct segments that may stay connected). No PATO term exists.

label: pinnatipartite
definition: A pinnatifid quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being cut more than halfway, but not fully, to the midrib into segments arranged on either side of it.
reason: Definition is correct, but parent PATO:0001786 split is too general. Pinnatipartite falls exactly under FLOPO:0991078 pinnatifid (incisions arranged pinnately that do not reach the midrib), so it should be a child of pinnatifid. PATO:0104362 dissected is a second choice that would sit next to pinnatisect.

label: pinnately lobed
definition: A lobed quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's lobes being arranged on either side of a central axis.
reason: Genus-differentia under PATO lobed and correct. It overlaps FLOPO:0991078 pinnatifid in many glossaries, so curators should not annotate the same statement with both. The class itself is fine.

label: palmately lobed
definition: A lobed quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's lobes radiating from a common point.
reason: Correct and well formed. PATO has no such term. The 'tuber' bearer is probably an extraction error and does not affect the class.

label: tripinnate
definition: A pinnate quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's secondary divisions (pinnules) being themselves pinnate, so that the bearer is three times pinnately divided.
reason: The meaning is right. The new wording follows the pattern of FLOPO:0991014 bipinnate (divisions themselves pinnate), so the two read as a series. The '3-pinnate' synonym fits.

label: pedate
definition: A dissected quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being palmately divided, with the outer lateral divisions divided again so that the segments arise along two curved side axes like a bird's foot.
reason: Meaning is right (Helleborus, Arisaema). PATO:0104362 dissected, the term already used for pinnatisect, is a closer parent than the general PATO:0001786 split. The 'vascular bundle' bearer reflects pedate venation, which the same wording covers.

label: trifoliolate
definition: A structural quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being a compound leaf with three leaflets.
reason: Meaning is right, but 'inhering in a leaf by virtue of its' does not follow the PATO wording. 'trifoliate' (strictly: with three leaves) is rightly only a related synonym. The parent matches FLOPO:0991073 unifoliolate.

label: excurrent
definition: A positional quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's extending beyond the apex or margin of the structure through which it runs.
reason: Two meanings in one class. The definition covers a midrib or costa running out as a mucro or awn. Floras also use 'excurrent' for tree form, meaning a main trunk that runs to the top of the crown (the 'whole plant' and 'stem' sense). That sense is a different quality and should be its own class or rejected. Bearers 'leaf', 'glume' and 'bract' are a different problem: they describe the part the vein runs out of, not the vein, and should be re-annotated to the costa or midvein.

label: percurrent
definition: A positional quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's extending through the whole length of the structure through which it runs, to its apex but not beyond.
bearers: costa|leaf|vascular bundle|tertiary leaf vein|leaf lamina|whole plant
reason: Two meanings in one class. The definition covers a costa or midrib reaching the apex. In leaf architecture (Manual of Leaf Architecture), 'percurrent' tertiary veins cross the space between neighbouring secondary veins, which is a different meaning (see the 'tertiary leaf vein' bearer). Split it or restrict the class. The 'whole plant' bearer is doubtful.

label: introrse
definition: An orientation quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's facing towards the centre of the flower, so that it opens (dehisces) towards it.
reason: Meaning is right. The new wording makes facing the core quality and opening a consequence of it, so the orientation parent fits better. Bearers 'sepal' and 'leaf lamina lobe' are probably extraction errors.

label: extrorse
definition: An orientation quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's facing away from the centre of the flower, so that it opens (dehisces) outwards.
reason: Mirror of introrse. Meaning is right. The 'radicle' bearer is outside the anther sense.

label: resupinate
definition: An inverted quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being turned upside down by a twist of its stalk.
reason: Correct for orchid flowers (twisted pedicel or ovary) and resupinate leaves (twisted petiole, as in Alstroemeria). It is a proper child of PATO inverted (reversed in position).

label: didynamous
definition: A structural quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's consisting of four stamens in two pairs of unequal length.
reason: Meaning is right, but it should use the standard PATO wording ('bearer's'). The bearer is the androecium, a set of stamens, not a single stamen, so annotations on 'stamen' should move to the androecium (PO).

label: moniliform
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being cylindrical with constrictions at regular intervals, like a string of beads.
reason: Standard meaning. PATO has no beaded shape term. 'torulose' (slightly and irregularly constricted) is rightly a related, not exact, synonym.

label: clawed
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being abruptly narrowed at the base into a stalk-like part.
reason: Correct for petals (claw versus limb). 'unguiculate' is an exact synonym. PATO has no such term.

label: crustaceous
definition: A texture quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being hard, thin and brittle.
reason: Matches glossary definitions of crustaceous for seed coats and endocarps. It combines PATO hard and brittle with thinness, so no single PATO term covers it.

label: comose
definition: A hairy quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's having a tuft of hairs at one end.
reason: Two meanings in one class. The hair sense (seeds with a coma, as in Asclepias and Epilobium) fits under hairy. Floras also say 'comose' for a terminal tuft of leaves or sterile bracts (crowns, pineapple and Muscari inflorescences), the sense behind the leaf, stem and whole-plant bearers. That sense is not hairy. Restrict the class to the hair sense and reject or separate the other.

label: stipitate-glandular
definition: A hairy quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being covered with stalked glands.
reason: Stalked glands are glandular trichomes, so it fits under hairy (hairlike projections). The meaning is standard. It is close to, but distinct from, glandular-pubescent.

label: glandular-pubescent
definition: A pubescent hair quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being covered with short soft hairs, at least some of which are tipped with a gland.
reason: The parent means covered with short hairs, so the definition should say so. 'glandular-hairy' does not imply short hairs and should be a related, not exact, synonym.

label: gland-dotted
definition: A punctate quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's surface being marked with dots that are glands on or within its tissue.
reason: Proper child of PATO punctate (marked with dots). The meaning is standard. 'pellucid-dotted' (translucent gland dots) is rightly a related synonym.

label: cauliflorous
definition: A positional quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's arising, or bearing flowers that arise, directly from the trunk or from older, leafless woody branches.
reason: Meaning is right, but 'inhering in a plant by virtue of its' does not follow the PATO wording. It also names only the plant, while most bearers are flowers, inflorescences and fruits. The new text covers both kinds of bearer.

label: cleistogamous
definition: A closed quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's remaining closed and being self-pollinated without opening.
reason: Meaning is right, but the wording ('inhering in a flower by virtue of its') does not follow the PATO pattern. The 'seed' bearer is probably from 'cleistogamous seed' (seed from cleistogamous flowers) and should go on the flower.

label: polygamous
definition: A phenotypic sex quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's producing both bisexual and unisexual flowers, on the same plant or on different plants of the species.
reason: Meaning and parent are right and match the siblings monoecious FLOPO:0991071, dioecious FLOPO:0991072 and unisexual FLOPO:0991015. The current text names only 'a plant', but floras also say 'inflorescences polygamous', and the standard glossary sense covers both plants and inflorescences. The generic bearer form fits that. A single flower cannot be polygamous, so the flower bearer is a mapping error.

label: heterogamous
definition: A phenotypic sex quality inhering in an inflorescence by virtue of the bearer's containing flowers of two or more sexual kinds, such as pistillate marginal and bisexual or functionally staminate central flowers of a capitulum.
reason: Wrong parent. Heterogamous (as opposed to homogamous) describes the sexual make-up of a head. It is a sex-expression quality like its near sibling polygamous FLOPO:0991177, which sits under phenotypic sex, not general structure. The definition is otherwise right.

label: scorpioid
definition: A coiled quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's tip being coiled in one plane like a scorpion's tail.
reason: Matches the usual descriptive sense: an axis, chiefly a cyme, curled at the tip like a scorpion's tail. PATO coiled is the right parent and PATO has no such term. The developmental sense (flowers alternately on opposite sides of a sympodium) belongs to the inflorescence type, not this quality.

label: fastigiate
definition: A positional quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being erect and close to the main axis, more or less parallel to it and to the others of its kind.
bearers: branch|stem|inflorescence|whole plant|plant ovary|higher order inflorescence axis
reason: Standard sense: branches or stems clustered, erect and parallel, as in a columnar tree. The parent position is acceptable and PATO has no such term. The plant ovary bearer is probably a mapping error.

label: marcescent
definition: A shedability quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's withering without being shed.
reason: Correct glossary sense: withering but persisting on the plant. It is the right sibling of PATO:0001731 deciduous (plant) under shedability. PATO has no such term.

label: saucer-shaped
definition: A concave 3-D shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being shaped like a saucer: round and shallowly concave.
reason: Correct: shallower than PATO:0040009 bowl shaped and PATO:0002227 cup-shaped, so it is not a duplicate. Patelliform is a fitting exact synonym.

label: flask-shaped
definition: A concave 3-D shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being shaped like a flask: swollen below and narrowed into a neck.
reason: Correct botanical sense (lageniform; ampulliform is close). A shape with a neck is non-convex, so it fits PATO's concave 3-D shape definition. PATO has no flask term.

label: plano-convex
definition: A convex quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being flat on one side and convex on the other.
reason: Correct, and it is the natural sibling of PATO:0002040 biconvex, which also sits under PATO:0001355 convex. PATO has no plano-convex term.

label: obtriangular
definition: A triangular quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's outline being triangular with one angle at the point of attachment and the broadest side distal.
reason: The current text never says the outline is triangular. As written it equally describes obovate or cuneate. The differentia must state the inverted triangle. Obdeltoid could be added as an exact synonym.

label: repand
definition: An edge shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's margin having shallow, irregular, rounded sinuses in the plane of the blade; weakly sinuate.
reason: 'Slightly and unevenly wavy' does not separate it from PATO:0000967 undulate (waves at right angles to the blade). Glossaries define repand as shallowly sinuate, in the plane of the blade. The parent edge shape is fine.

label: coherent
definition: An attachment quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's sticking to other structures of the same kind without being fused with them.
reason: This is the common flora sense (anthers coherent into a tube; petals coherent at the tips). It is distinct from connate FLOPO:0991067, which means true fusion. Some glossaries use 'coherent' loosely for 'connate', so statements stay ambiguous, but the class itself is sound.

label: adherent
definition: An attachment quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's sticking to a structure of a different kind without being fused with it.
reason: The correct counterpart of coherent (unlike parts, not fused) and distinct from adnate. It is not PATO:0002331 adhesive, which is the sticky surface disposition.

label: distant
definition: A positional quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being widely separated from the nearest structures of its kind.
reason: Correct flora sense (leaves or spikelets distant, i.e. widely spaced along the axis). PATO:0002233 far from is relational and needs an explicit second entity. This monadic spacing quality among structures of the same kind is not a duplicate, like connivent FLOPO:0991147.

label: approximate
definition: A positional quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being close to the nearest structures of its kind without being joined to them.
reason: Correct glossary sense: close together but not united. It is the opposite of distant FLOPO:0991189. PATO:0002259 adjacent to is relational and needs a named second entity, so this is not a duplicate.

label: axile
definition: A positional quality inhering in a placenta or its ovules by virtue of their being borne on the central axis of an ovary that is divided into locules.
reason: Standard definition of axile placentation. The parent position fits. The stipule bearer is a mapping error ('stipules axillary'?) and should be checked.

label: parietal
definition: A positional quality inhering in a placenta or its ovules by virtue of their being borne on the wall of the ovary.
reason: Standard definition of parietal placentation. Correct and well formed.

label: emergent
definition: A positional quality inhering in a plant or plant structure by virtue of its rising above the surface of the water in which the plant is rooted.
reason: The definition is right for the aquatic sense (sibling of submerged FLOPO:0991044 and floating FLOPO:0991045). But the word has a second common flora sense: projecting just beyond an enclosing structure, as in 'capsule emergent from the perichaetial leaves or calyx', which is close to exserted. A third sense is a tree rising above the canopy. The fruit and capsule bearers show the second sense is being mapped here. The aquatic class should keep this definition, with a context rule: only when water is mentioned, or for a whole plant, leaf or inflorescence of an aquatic.

label: radiate
definition: A structural quality inhering in a capitulum by virtue of its having ray flowers surrounding the disc flowers.
reason: The definition is correct for the Asteraceae head. But the leaf, leaf lamina and petal bearers show the general sense 'spreading outward from a common centre' (veins, spines, stellate hairs, petals radiate), which is a different quality. The class must be restricted by rule to capitulum or inflorescence bearers. The general sense should not map here; at most it maps to a spreading/position term.

label: disciform
definition: A structural quality inhering in a capitulum by virtue of its having only tubular flowers, the outer ones pistillate with a very slender corolla.
reason: The definition is correct for the Asteraceae disciform head. But most bearers (stigma, calyx, fruit, tuber, cotyledon) use the other sense, 'disc-shaped: flat and circular', which is a shape, not a head structure. Restrict this class by rule to capitulum bearers. Map the shape sense elsewhere (a flat circular shape term), not to this class.

label: crested
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's having an elevated, irregular or toothed ridge.
reason: Correct glossary sense (cristate). PATO:0002358 ridged exists, but its definition is poor and crests are often fringed or toothed appendages (Polygala keel petal, seed crests), not simple ridges. So keeping it under shape rather than ridged is defensible.

label: raceme-like
definition: A structural quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's branching pattern resembling a raceme, an unbranched indeterminate inflorescence of stalked flowers.
reason: Wrong parent. PATO shape means ratios of distances between features. Resembling a raceme is a matter of branching pattern and the arrangement of flowers, which PATO's structure definition covers (arrangement and connectivity of parts). Same correction for panicle-like and thyrse-like. The definition is otherwise right; 'indeterminate' sharpens it.

label: panicle-like
definition: A structural quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's branching pattern resembling a panicle, a much-branched inflorescence with stalked flowers on the branches.
reason: Same as raceme-like: this is an inflorescence branching pattern, so the parent should be structure, not shape. The meaning is right.

label: thyrse-like
definition: A structural quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's branching pattern resembling a thyrse, an inflorescence with an indeterminate main axis and cymose lateral branches.
reason: Same as raceme-like: this is a branching pattern, so the parent should be structure. The definition and synonyms (thyrsoid, thyrsiform) are correct.

label: bract-like
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being reduced, small and leaf-like or scale-like, resembling a bract.
reason: 'Similarity to the appearance of a bract' is circular and vague. In floras, bract-like (bracteiform) means reduced, small, leaf- or scale-like (sepals bract-like, reduced upper leaves bract-like). The differentia should say so.

label: pinnately veined
definition: A branched quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's venation having a single primary vein from which the secondary veins arise on either side along its length.
reason: The meaning is right (penninerved) and consistent with sibling triplinerved FLOPO:0991202 under branched. It is not PATO:0000410 pinnate, which is about leaflets. The text should say it is the venation of the bearer, and add 'along its length' to separate it from palmate and triplinerved venation.

label: triplinerved
definition: A branched quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's having three main veins, the two lateral ones arising from the midvein above the base.
reason: Matches the strict botanical sense: the laterals leave the midvein a little above the base, which separates it from 3-nerved (all three from the base). The parent matches its sibling FLOPO:0991201 pinnately veined. PATO has no venation-pattern term.

label: alveolate
definition: A texture quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's surface being marked with close-set angular depressions like a honeycomb.
reason: Standard glossary sense (honeycombed; angular pits separated by thin walls). Not the same as PATO:0002296 foveate (small, shallow, regular pits, not honeycomb-like) or PATO:0002294 scrobiculate (oblong, trench-like pits). Its sibling texture classes support the parent. The bearer 'vascular bundle' in the data is doubtful, but that is a problem with the annotations, not with the class.

label: scalariform
definition: A spatial pattern quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's parts, such as veins, bars, pits or thickenings, being arranged in parallel transverse rows like the rungs of a ladder.
reason: The meaning and parent are right. But 'marked with ... bars' reads like a surface marking. In floras the term mostly describes tertiary veins that form the rungs between secondaries, and also ladder-like pitting or perforation plates. The pattern is how the parts are arranged, which also fits the PATO spatial pattern definition (repeated placement of parts).

label: ruminate
definition: A texture quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being irregularly furrowed and infolded, often by ingrowths of a surrounding layer such as the seed coat, so that its surface or cut face looks mottled, as if chewed.
reason: The main flora use is ruminate endosperm or seed (e.g. Annonaceae, Myristicaceae, palms). Here the testa grows into the endosperm, and the pattern shows on a cut face, not only on the outer surface. The current text covers only surface grooving. PATO texture is defined on surface elements, so the parent is acceptable but loose; there is no better PATO parent. Not the same as PATO:0001359 rugose or PATO:0001810 wrinkled, which are surface creases.

label: streaked
definition: A multi-colored quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being marked with narrow, irregular lines of a different colour.
reason: Correct colour-pattern sense, a sibling of PATO:0000333 spotted and PATO:0002274 mottled. 'Irregular' keeps it apart from PATO:0001946 banded (exact synonym 'striped'), which is regular stripes, and from PATO:0001410 striated, which is a shape quality (lines or grooves).

label: descending
definition: An oblique orientation quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being directed obliquely downward.
reason: This is the exact opposite of PATO:0104355 ascending (directed gradually upward at an oblique angle), under the same parent. Not a duplicate of PATO:0002237 retrorse (curved), PATO:0104353 reflexed (bent abruptly) or PATO pendent (hanging down by its own weight).

label: marginal
definition: A peripheral quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being located at or on the margin of the flattened structure that bears it.
reason: PATO:0002107 peripheral ('at the edge or boundary of a related entity') already covers this meaning. 'Marginal' is its narrower botanical case: on the margin of a flat organ (marginal sori, marginal placentation along the carpel suture). In floras, 'peripheral' also means 'toward the outside' (e.g. peripheral bundles in a stem cross-section), so it should not simply be merged into peripheral. Instead, move it under peripheral rather than the bare 'position'.

label: barbed
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's bearing short, stiff, sharp projections (barbs) that point back towards its base, like the barbs of a fish-hook or arrow-head.
reason: The meaning is right, but 'point backward' is unclear for organs with no front or back; botanically, the barbs point back toward the bearer's base. 'Glochidiate' (bearing glochids, barbed bristles) fits as a related synonym. PATO:0001365 spiny is the nearest PATO term but says nothing about direction, so it is not a duplicate. Shape is a broad but acceptable parent.

label: spine-tipped
definition: A pointed quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's ending in a spine.
reason: Standard glossary sense (apex ending in a spine; 'spinose-tipped' is a fitting synonym). Not a duplicate of PATO:0001973 cuspidate (tapering gradually into a rigid point) or FLOPO:0991055 mucronulate (a minute, non-spiny point). PATO:0002258 pointed is the right parent.
